title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. This page tries to build, from cochain algebras, a realization functor back to simplicial sets, in the style of Sullivan's spatial realization, and tests it on the circle.

(1) Definition. For a simplicial set X_*, take the cochains C^.(X_*) with their multiplicative structure (cup product) and differential d. Set
  F_*(X_*) = [ n -> Hom_mult(C^.(X_*), C^.(Delta^n_*)) ].
This is the simplicial set of multiplicative dg maps into the cochains of the standard simplices. It is the analogue of Sullivan's <A> = Hom_cdga(A, Omega^*_poly(Delta^.)). Here the simplicial model of forms is the combinatorial cochain object C^.(Delta^*_*) rather than polynomial forms.

(2) Notation. L_n is the rank-(n+1) module attached to the vertices of Delta^n. The cochains of Delta^n are written [L_n -> Lambda^1 L_n -> ...]; for Delta^1 this gives L_1 = k^2 and 'Lambda^1 L_1' = k. Psi_m is apparently the augmentation-type piece, with a sequence 0 -> Psi_m^v (x) L_* -> L_m^v (x) L_* -> L_* -> 0.

(3) Representable case. He computes P^m_* := F_*(Delta^m_*).
- Unit-preserving linear maps Hom(L_m, L_*) form a torsor under Psi_m^v (x) L_* =: L^m_*.
- Hence P^m_* is an affine m-space over the simplicial module L_*, built inductively as P^m_* = P^{m-1}_*(T).
- Explicitly, a degree-0 generator goes to alpha T_m and the degree-1 part to T_m beta, with alpha in k and beta in Psi_m. The side computations with T_0, T_1, eta, T_1 o eta, eta o eta compose such maps (structure maps L_m -> L_n, T_m -> T_n).
- There is a Yoneda-type comparison Delta^m_n = Hom_ens(Delta^n, Delta^m) -> P^m_n, together with an arrow written 'Delta^m_* ->~ P^m_*' whose meaning is unclear (see errors).

(4) General X. Since C^.(X) = lim over the simplex category Delta/X of C^.(Delta^m), there is a chain
  X = colim Delta^m_*  ->  colim_{Delta/X} P^m_* = colim Hom(C^.(Delta^m), C^.(Delta^*_*))  ->  Hom(lim C^.(Delta^m), C^.(Delta^*_*)) = F_*(X).
He asks of the last arrow: 'non une équivalence d'homotopie ?' This is the key question: does Hom out of a limit commute with the colimit up to homotopy?

(5) Test case: the circle. X = Coker(Delta^0 ⇉ Delta^1) = S^1, and C^.(X) = Ker(C^.(Delta^1) ⇉ C^.(Delta^0)) = [0 -> k --0--> k -> 0 -> ...]. The induced multiplicative structure is trivial on the degree-1 class. So F_n(S^1) = Hom([k -> k], [L_n -> Lambda^1 L_n -> ...]): the unit goes to 1 and the degree-1 generator goes to any 1-cocycle beta. Thus F_*(S^1) ≅ Z^1(C^.(Delta^*); k), which by Dold–Kan is a K(k,1).

Purpose: test whether multiplicative cochain data over an arbitrary ring k (with divided powers in mind) recover a 'k-localized' homotopy type, as Sullivan theory does over Q.
errors: The circle computation is consistent: it gives K(k,1), the right answer for k = Q. For k = F_p or Z it gives K(F_p,1) or K(Z,1), not the p-completion K(Z_p,1). This is the known failure of naive (non-E-infinity, Frobenius-ignoring) cochain realization in characteristic p. The page does not address it.
Cup-product cochains are not graded-commutative. 'Hom with multiplicative structure' must therefore mean associative dg-algebra maps (or some PD-commutative replacement), and that is not specified.

The arrow written 'Delta^m_* ->~ P^m_*' cannot literally be an isomorphism: P^m_n is an affine space over L_n, not a finite set. It is presumably meant as a weak equivalence or contractibility claim, which is left unproved.
The comparison colim P^m_* -> F_*(X) is explicitly left open ('équiv. d'homotopie ?').

ideas.what: Realization functor X -> [n -> Hom_mult(C^.(X), C^.(Delta^n))] recovering a homotopy type from its multiplicative cochains over an arbitrary ring k
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan spatial realization / Bousfield–Gugenheim adjunction; integral or p-adic analogues (Mandell's E-infinity cochain theorem, Toën's affine stacks)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) discusses 'schématisation' of homotopy types in spirit, but not this cochain-realization computation

ideas.what: Realization of the standard simplex as an affine space (torsor) over the simplicial module L_*, P^m = P^{m-1}(T), with Yoneda map Delta^m -> P^m
ideas.modern_name: contractible algebraic simplices / simplicial affine spaces used in cosimplicial-algebra models

ideas.what: Circle test: Hom(C^.(S^1), C^.(Delta^*)) = Z^1, a K(k,1)
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan computation of the realization of a free cochain algebra on a degree-1 class

missed.claim: Around 1976, in the PD de Rham notes, Grothendieck was setting up a Sullivan-type realization of homotopy types from multiplicative cochains over a general ring k. He explicitly left open whether colim over Delta/X of P^m is homotopy equivalent to Hom(lim C^.(Delta^m), C^.(Delta^*)). This predates his Pursuing Stacks remarks on schematic homotopy types and Toën's affine stacks.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that the 'affine/schematic homotopy type' programme (later Toën; Mandell in the E-infinity setting) was already being tested by Grothendieck in 1975-76, in connection with divided-power de Rham complexes. The latter are an integral substitute for Sullivan's polynomial forms.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics itself is routine: a Sullivan-style realization and the circle giving K(k,1). It is historically notable as an early, little-documented instance of Grothendieck testing cochain-algebra realization over general k within the 1976 PD de Rham material. Nothing here is a finished new result.
transcription_corrections: The limit in 'F_*(X_*) = Hom(lim C^.(Delta^m_*), C^.(Delta^*_*))' is an inverse limit over Ob(Delta/X_*). The following lines are direct limits: colim Hom(C^.(Delta^m), C^.(Delta^*)) = colim P^m_*, and colim Delta^m_* over Delta/X_*.
The query under the first arrow reads 'non une équiv. d'homotopie ?'.
The circle's cochain complex is written [0 -> k --0--> k -> 0 -> 0 -> ...] with the note '(structure mult. induite par C^.(Delta^1_*))'.
The side computation reads 'alpha T_m <-| alpha T_1' and 'T_m beta <-| 1' with '(beta in Psi_m)'. The bottom-left line 'beta in T' may be 'beta in Psi'.
